stem: How much on-chip program memory (ROM) does the 8051 have?
explanation: It has 4 KB on-chip ROM within a 64 KB program address space.
source: Case Studies Microprocessors and Microcontrollers.pptx, Unit 4

stem: How many I/O lines does the 8051 have?
explanation: Ports P0 to P3 have eight pins each.
source: Case Studies Microprocessors and Microcontrollers.pptx, Unit 4

stem: With EA = 0, the 8051 fetches program code only from external ROM.
explanation: EA = 1 allows internal and external program memory.
source: Case Studies Microprocessors and Microcontrollers.pptx, Unit 4

stem: Which 8051 port also serves as the multiplexed low-order address and data bus?
explanation: With ALE = 1 Port 0 carries A0–A7; with ALE = 0 it carries data.
source: Case Studies Microprocessors and Microcontrollers.pptx, Unit 4

explanation: The 20-bit address bus belongs to the 8086.
source: Case Studies Microprocessors and Microcontrollers.pptx, Unit 4; Unit 1

stem: Which registers can be used for register indirect addressing in the 8051?
explanation: Only R0 and R1 can hold addresses, written with '@'.
source: Case Studies Microprocessors and Microcontrollers.pptx, Unit 4

stem: Which one is not an 8051 instruction group?
explanation: The five groups are arithmetic, logical, data transfer, Boolean and branching.
source: Case Studies Microprocessors and Microcontrollers.pptx, Unit 4

stem: The 8031 is a ROM-less version of the 8051.
explanation: Adding external ROM to it uses up two ports.
source: Case Studies Microprocessors and Microcontrollers.pptx, Unit 4
